paper_topic: Jacobian regularization on Recurrent-Depth VLA (RD-VLA) for depth-extrapolatable robot policies on LIBERO-10

nodes.text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for building generalist robot policies that can interpret natural language instructions and execute complex manipulation tasks (Brohan et al., 2022; 2023; Kim et al., 2024; Black et al., 2024).
nodes.display_label: VLA models for generalist robot policies

nodes.text: By leveraging pretrained vision-language models, these systems can transfer semantic knowledge from web-scale data to robotic control, enabling more flexible and generalizable robot behaviors.
nodes.display_label: VLMs transfer semantic knowledge to control

nodes.text: A key limitation of standard VLA architectures is their fixed computational depth: the same amount of compute is expended regardless of task complexity.
nodes.display_label: Standard VLAs have fixed compute depth

nodes.text: RD-VLA (Tur et al., 2026) addresses this by introducing a recurrent action head that enables test-time compute scaling through iterative latent refinement.

By unrolling a weight-tied transformer block to arbitrary depth K, RD-VLA can dynamically allocate compute based on task difficulty, achieving significant improvements on challenging manipulation tasks.
However, RD-VLA reports a "depth boundary" phenomenon where performance degrades at high iteration counts (K > 24), limiting the practical utility of depth extrapolation.
nodes.display_label: Depth boundary degrades performance at K>24

nodes.text: This instability resembles challenges observed in other iterative computation frameworks, such as Deep Equilibrium Models (DEQ) (Bai et al., 2019) and Universal Transformers (Dehghani et al., 2018), where unbounded iteration can lead to divergent or oscillatory behavior.
We investigate Jacobian regularization (Bai et al., 2021) as a principled approach to encourage contractive dynamics in the RD-VLA recurrent core.

By penalizing the Frobenius norm of the state-to-state Jacobian, we aim to ensure that the recurrent mapping is a contraction, guaranteeing convergence to a unique fixed point regardless of iteration depth.
Surprisingly, our experiments on LIBERO-10 (Liu et al., 2023) reveal that the depth boundary phenomenon does not manifest in this setting.
Both baseline and Jacobian-regularized RD-VLA exhibit 0% overthinking with flat MSE curves across depths K = 4 to K = 128.
This suggests that the depth boundary may be benchmark-specific or evaluation-protocol-dependent, rather than an inherent limitation of the architecture.

Empirical evidence of benchmark-specific depth boundary: We demonstrate that the overthinking phenomenon reported in RD-VLA does not occur on LIBERO-10 with offline teacher-forced evaluation, informing future research on when and why depth boundaries manifest.

Two-phase training for Jacobian regularization: We propose a training strategy that achieves 1.6% MSE improvement with 15× efficiency gain over from-scratch regularization, by fine-tuning a converged baseline with gentle Jacobian penalty.
Adaptive stopping analysis: We show that the RD-VLA recurrent core converges within 6 iterations on average, enabling 50% compute savings at inference through early termination.

observations: FA0013 is a single-anchor empirical investigation. The narrative arc opens with broad VLA context (N1-N3): N3, while phrased as 'A key limitation', is paper-theme-aligned field-level framing (the paper IS about depth extrapolation, so 'fixed computational depth' is the topic-of-study being introduced, not a critique of any specific named Prior_Work) and is therefore typed Context per the Pass-3 / Stage-2 paper-theme rule. The anchor RD-VLA (N4-N5) is then introduced as the solution to that gap. A second contrast (N6) flips the anchor's success story by surfacing the 'depth boundary' instability — this IS a real Limitation (it critiques the named PW N4), and an analogy to DEQ/Universal Transformers (N7) generalizes the limitation. The Method block (N8-N9) proposes Jacobian regularization as a principled remedy with explicit cross-segment lexical link to 'depth boundary' / 'contractive dynamics', motivating two addresses edges into N6. The Result block (N10-N12) contains a striking null result — the predicted depth boundary fails to appear on LIBERO-10 — that the authors reframe as benchmark-specificity rather than as invalidation of the method. The Contribution block (C1-C3) is a fork-fed by N9 for the methodological findings (C2, C3) plus a separate consequence edge N12 → C1 that promotes the null observation into Finding 1. Topology features one main spine, an early consequence-driven step at N3 → N4 (gap → anchor), a contrast pivot at N5 → N6, and a method-rooted Contribution fan-out. The intro is unusually self-critical: the paper's own data undermines the named motivation, and the contributions retitle that absence as the principal finding.
